sources_considered.why: Readable reporting of IDC's target-quarter estimates. Used as context because its buyer group and asset coverage differ from the claim.
The underlying IDC release returned HTTP 403. The accessible news report is identified as a secondary source.
Primary economic research explains why company capex totals cannot simply be classified as AI spending.

evidence_items.locator: Paragraph beginning “By the way, in Q2”
evidence_items.explanation: The report attributes 86.7% of second-quarter AI infrastructure spending to hyperscalers, cloud builders and neoclouds. That broader group and its server-and-storage purchases do not establish the four named companies' share of all AI capex.

metric_scope.company: Global hyperscalers, cloud builders and neoclouds
metric_scope.metric: AI server and storage infrastructure spending

evidence_items.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
evidence_items.locator: Firm Investment and Adoption, discussion preceding Figure 4
evidence_items.explanation: The researchers identify an attribution problem with using hyperscaler capex as an AI investment measure. Their analysis does not provide the required target-quarter share or quantify systemic risk from the four companies.

unresolved_gaps: No comparable target-quarter numerator and denominator isolating the four companies' AI capex were found.
The accessible concentration estimate includes other cloud providers and excludes portions of capital expenditure.
No analysis found establishes the magnitude of US systemic exposure attributable specifically to this four-company concentration.
